Search the NCT03434379 protocol and report all listed exclusion criteria with supporting passages; if a document id is necessary and not available, say so.","rationale":"The registry resolved IMbrave150 to NCT03434379, but returned no docId; the criteria themselves are protocol text, so search using the identified NCT number rather than assume a document identifier.","result_shape":"passages","succeeded":true}],"decision":{"answerable":true,"entities":["NCT03434379"],"clarifying_question":"","note":"IMbrave150 resolved to NCT03434379; protocol search returned 14 passages concerning its exclusion criteria. The graph did not return a docId, so the search used the NCT number."},"render_target":"none","composed_answer":"**IMbrave150 excluded patients who met any of the medical, liver-cancer, bleeding-risk, or recent-treatment criteria in its protocol.** The criteria applied to **NCT03434379**, the phase III study of atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus sorafenib in untreated locally advanced or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

The protocol’s Section 4.1.2 lists these exclusions:

- **Cancer and liver-related conditions:** Fibrolamellar HCC, sarcomatoid HCC, or mixed cholangiocarcinoma and HCC; moderate or severe ascites; hepatic encephalopathy; HBV and HCV coinfection; uncontrolled tumor-related pain; and certain uncontrolled effusions or ascites requiring recurrent drainage. Symptomatic, untreated, or actively progressing CNS metastases and a history of leptomeningeal disease were excluded. The protocol allows some treated, asymptomatic CNS lesions if its specified conditions are met.
- **Varices and bleeding risk:** Untreated or incompletely treated esophageal or gastric varices with bleeding or high bleeding risk; a variceal bleed within **6 months**; significant coagulopathy or bleeding tendency; recent hemoptysis; and specified recent use of high-dose aspirin, antiplatelet drugs, therapeutic anticoagulants, or thrombolytics. Patients had to undergo an esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) so varices could be assessed and treated, unless they had undergone one within **6 months** before treatment.
- **Other medical conditions:** Active or prior autoimmune disease or immune deficiency, with specified exceptions; certain pneumonitis or pulmonary-fibrosis histories; active tuberculosis; serious infection; significant cardiovascular or vascular disease; inadequately controlled hypertension (**systolic BP ≥ 150 mmHg and/or diastolic BP > 100 mmHg**); long-QT or uncorrectable electrolyte disorders; uncontrolled or symptomatic hypercalcemia; and a prior malignancy other than HCC within **5 years**, subject to specified exceptions. Prior allogeneic stem-cell or solid-organ transplantation was also excluded.
- **Bevacizumab-related surgical and gastrointestinal risks:** Recent major surgery, biopsy, trauma, or certain abdominal procedures; recent gastrointestinal perforation, fistula, abscess, obstruction, or intra-abdominal inflammation; unexplained abdominal free air; serious non-healing wounds, active ulcers, or untreated fractures; and metastatic disease involving major airways or blood vessels or certain large central mediastinal masses. The protocol permits portal- or hepatic-vein vascular invasion.
- **Prior or recent treatments:** Prior CD137 agonists or immune-checkpoint blockade; recent investigational therapy, systemic immunostimulants or immunosuppressants, live attenuated vaccine, therapeutic antibiotics, strong CYP3A4 inducers, radiotherapy, or local liver therapy; and chronic daily NSAID treatment. The protocol specifies time windows and exceptions for several of these.
- **Other exclusions:** Severe allergic reactions to chimeric or humanized antibodies or fusion proteins; hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or components of atezolizumab or bevacizumab; pregnancy, breastfeeding, or plans to become pregnant within the specified post-treatment periods; and another condition that contraindicated an investigational drug, could affect interpretation of results, or put the patient at high risk of treatment complications.

These are the protocol’s exclusions; several have detailed exceptions and timing rules in Section 4.1.2 (pages 54–58).","usage":{"input_tokens":10367,"cached_input_tokens":9531,"output_tokens":426,"total_tokens":10793,"llm_calls":3,"model_id":"gpt-6-sol"}}
